query: Emerging evidence in diverse animal models suggests that gut bacteria may modulate amyloid-driven diseases, not only in synucleinopathy as we and others describe, but Alzheimer's disease (Harach et al., 2017; Dodiya et al., 2019) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) as well (Blacher et al., 2019), providing justification for future human studies and revealing possible new targets for interventions that may prevent, slow, or halt amyloid formation and neurodegenerative disease.
